correctness.rationale: For m≥2 matrices and commuting positive moduli P_k, choose a common orthonormal eigenbasis e_j with P_ke_j=p_kj e_j. Each column v_j=(Σ A_k)e_j has norm≤s_j=Σp_kj. For 1≤p≤2, Schur–Horn and concavity t^{p/2} give Tr[(T*T)^{p/2}]≤Σ||v_j||^p≤Σs_j^p=||ΣP_k||_p^p. At 1≤p<2, strict concavity forces orthogonality of the nonzero output columns and Euclidean triangle equality forces the same polar direction for each j, giving exactly a common left partial isometry V on supp S; converse immediate. At p=2 only within-column alignment is necessary. For p≥2 write T=(ΣU_k W_k)S, where W_k are normalized diagonal weights; the linear map from diagonal D to (ΣU_kW_k)D has ℓ2→S2 norm≤1 and ℓ∞→S∞ norm≤√m. Complex interpolation gives m^(1/2−1/p) for all p≥2. Taking A_k=e1 e_k* with n=m and the positive aligned witness attains optimal constants. A separate independently generated bounded random SVD test (m=2,3,4; n=2,5; p=1,1.3,2,3,5,9) passed; it does not prove the general theorem.

The narrower theorem is not obtained merely by setting noncommuting terms to zero in any inspected general coefficient.
